correctness.rationale: All finite, simple, labeled rook graphs K_m square K_n with m,n>=2 are covered. The line-graph equivalence proves induced forests correspond exactly to bipartite linear forests. The key maximality lemma compares low-degree opposite-side endpoints in different components and yields the balanced Hamilton-path versus unbalanced two-regular-smaller-side dichotomy. Normalized bipartite path counts and labeled exponential formula prove all size coefficients; n!/c! with c=n-m and m! labels proves the facet count. Direct graph-based exhaustive validation on 370512 candidate subsets across ten profiles agrees coefficientwise; this is supporting finite evidence rather than an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The finding determines every face and facet cardinality of a natural infinite two-parameter simplicial complex, proves the nontrivial purity/greedy-extension property, gives an exact normalized EGF and labeled maximal-set census, and explains a sharp Hamilton-path versus contracted-linear-forest structural transition at equal side sizes. This is motivated by the well-f-coveredness question and connected induced-tree literature, not an arbitrary finite instance or renaming.
